title: COS 101 ( UNIZIK ) : BRIEF INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTING
subject: COS 101

questions.question: A computer is defined as an electronic device that accepts data and processes it to produce which of the following?
questions.explanation: A computer processes data to produce meaningful information useful to humans.

questions.question: The term computer is derived from which Latin word?
questions.explanation: Computer comes from the Latin word computare which means to calculate.

questions.question: The manual method of data processing involves the use of which tools?
questions.explanation: The manual method uses chalk, wall, pen, pencil and similar tools.

questions.question: The mechanical method of data processing involves the use of which machines?
questions.explanation: The mechanical method uses machines like typewriters and adding machines.

questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer refers to its ability to perform completely different types of work at the same time?
questions.explanation: Versatility means computers are multipurpose and can perform different tasks simultaneously.

questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it does not suffer from tiredness or lack of concentration?
questions.explanation: Reliability means the computer performs consistently without human traits like tiredness.

questions.question: The first generation of computers used which technology?
questions.explanation: First generation computers used vacuum tube technology from 1940 to 1956.

questions.question: ENIAC was developed by which two individuals?
questions.explanation: John Presper Eckert and John Mauchly developed ENIAC at the University of Pennsylvania.

questions.question: UNIVAC I was the first commercially produced computer in which country?
questions.explanation: UNIVAC I was the first commercially produced computer in the US.

questions.question: The second generation of computers used which technology?
questions.explanation: Second generation computers used transistors from 1956 to 1963.

questions.question: Which programming languages were developed during the second generation?
questions.explanation: FORTRAN and COBOL were high-level languages developed during the second generation.

questions.question: The third generation of computers used which technology?
questions.explanation: Third generation computers used integrated circuits from 1964 to 1971.

questions.question: Which computer was a family of compatible computers that could run the same software?
questions.explanation: IBM System/360 was a family of compatible computers facilitating upgrades and scalability.

questions.question: The fourth generation of computers used which technology?
questions.explanation: Fourth generation computers used microprocessors based on VLSI technology.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a fourth generation computer?
questions.explanation: Apple II introduced in 1977 is an example of a fourth generation computer.

questions.question: The fifth generation of computers is characterized by which technology?
questions.explanation: Fifth generation computers use AI and microprocessor chips based on ULSI technology.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advancement expected in sixth generation computers?
questions.explanation: Quantum computing, nanotechnology and biocomputing are key advancements for sixth generation.

questions.question: Computers are classified based on which three criteria?
questions.explanation: Computers are classified by type, size and purpose.

questions.question: Which classification of computers includes analog, digital and hybrid?
questions.explanation: By type, computers are classified as analog, digital and hybrid.

questions.question: Which classification of computers includes micro, mini, mainframe and super?
questions.explanation: By size, computers are classified as micro, mini, mainframe and super computers.

questions.question: Which classification of computers includes general purpose and special purpose?
questions.explanation: By purpose, computers are classified as general purpose and special purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following is a core component of a computer system?
questions.explanation: CPU, motherboard, power supply, RAM and ROM are core components.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a peripheral device?
questions.explanation: Keyboard, mouse, monitor, printer and scanner are peripheral devices.

questions.question: Which part of the CPU executes arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit executes all arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question: Which part of the CPU controls and coordinates computer components?
questions.explanation: The Control Unit controls and coordinates computer components.

questions.question: Which type of memory is volatile and loses data when power is turned off?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile and data is erased once power supply is turned off.

questions.question: Which type of memory is permanent and does not allow data to be modified?
questions.explanation: ROM is a permanent form of storage that does not allow data modification.

questions.question: Which storage device uses laser light to read or write data?
questions.explanation: Optical disc drives use laser light to read or write data to optical discs.

questions.question: What is the maximum storage capacity of a Blu-ray disc?
questions.explanation: Blu-ray discs can store up to 50 GB of data.

questions.question: Which component acts as the central electrical circuit connecting different parts of the computer?
questions.explanation: The motherboard acts as the central electrical circuit connecting different parts.

questions.question: Which device provides electricity that activates the entire computer system?
questions.explanation: The power supply port provides electricity that activates the entire computer system.

questions.question: Which input device is used to input text, characters and commands?
questions.explanation: The keyboard is used to input text, characters and other important commands.

questions.question: Which output device generates a copy of virtual text or images on paper using ink?
questions.explanation: The printer generates a copy of virtual text or images on paper using ink.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an input device?
questions.explanation: Scanner is an input device that sends data to a computer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an output device?
questions.explanation: Monitor is an output device that displays information from the computer.

questions.question: Which unit is described as the main unit of a PC that contains the motherboard, processor and memory?
questions.explanation: The system unit contains the motherboard, processor, buses, memory and power supply.

questions.question: CPU speed is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: CPU speed is measured in megahertz which equals one million ticks per second.

questions.question: Which type of keyboard is used for special purpose applications requiring faster data entry?
questions.explanation: Special purpose keyboards are used for applications like ATMs requiring faster data entry.

questions.question: Which printer type combines a magnetic roller with powdered ink called toner?
questions.explanation: Laser printers use a magnetic roller with toner to transfer characters onto a page.

questions.question: Which printer type is the cheapest available and uses a print head to strike an inked ribbon?
questions.explanation: Dot-matrix printers are the cheapest and create characters by hammering pins against an inked ribbon.

questions.question: Which type of scanner looks and behaves like a photocopier?
questions.explanation: Flatbed scanners look and behave like a photocopier where items are laid on a glass plate.

questions.question: Which operating system type allows users to submit jobs to a central place with no interaction during processing?
questions.explanation: Batch processing collects jobs into a batch with no user interaction during processing.

questions.question: Which operating system type provides computing services to many users concurrently online?
questions.explanation: Time sharing operating systems provide computing services to many users concurrently online.

questions.question: Which operating system type is designed for applications where response time is critical to prevent disaster?
questions.explanation: Real time operating systems service applications where response time is of the essence.

questions.question: Which operating system component is responsible for creation and deletion of user and system processes?
questions.explanation: Process management handles creation, deletion, suspension and resumption of processes.

questions.question: Which type of software is designed to solve problems of a specific nature?
questions.explanation: Application software is designed to solve problems of a specific nature.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of application software?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Word is a word processing application software.

questions.question: Humanware is the combination of hardware and software elements that make which aspect as good as possible?
questions.explanation: Humanware aims to make human interaction with a device as good as possible.

questions.question: The internet originated from which network developed by the US Department of Defense?
questions.explanation: The internet originated from ARPANET in the late 1960s.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an internet application for communication?
questions.explanation: Email is a fast and reliable way to send messages globally through the internet.
